hero.oneLiner: India-based technology-enabled diagnostic services provider operating radiology, clinical laboratory and nuclear medicine centres across seven states through hospital-partnership and standalone models.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India-based technology-enabled diagnostic services provider operating radiology, clinical laboratory and nuclear medicine centres across seven states through hospital-partnership and standalone models.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Pramodini Medicare Limited provides technology-enabled diagnostic services - radiology (MRI, CT scan, X-ray, ultrasound with colour doppler, mammography, DEXA scan, intervention radiology and teleradiology), clinical laboratory (haematology, micro-biology, immunology, pathology and bio-chemistry) and nuclear medicine (PET-CT, SPECT and nuclear therapy) - to public hospitals, private hospitals, PSUs of the Government of India and medical colleges across tier I, II and III cities. It operates 16 diagnostic centres across 7 states and 14 cities in India through four partnership models (Public Private Partnership, Private Private Partnership, Strategic Partnership with PSUs, and standalone Private Centres), together with a processing unit-cum-laboratory and 24x7 teleradiology hub at its registered office in Vijayawada.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Infer Radiological and Imaging Services Private Limited — Group Company: Related party transactions per Restated Consolidated Financial Statements; also linked to Promoter Dr. Chalasani Kavitha
- Vista Pramodini Medicare Private Limited — Group Company: Incorporated pursuant to MOU with Vista Imaging & Medical Centre Private Limited
- Sri Ram Medicare Private Limited — Corporate Promoter

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Radiology:** MRI, CT Scan, X-ray, Ultrasound with colour doppler, Mammography, Dexa Scan, Intervention Radiology, Teleradiology
- **Clinical Laboratory:** Haematology, Micro-Biology, Immunology, Pathology & Bio-Chemistry
- **Nuclear Medicine:** PET-CT, SPECT, Nuclear therapy

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Public Private Partnership - government hospitals & teaching hospitals (54.19% of FY26 revenue)
- Private Private Partnership - private sector hospitals (20.82% of FY26 revenue)
- Private Centres / standalone (17.72% of FY26 revenue)
- Strategic Partnership with PSU Govt of India (7.27% of FY26 revenue)

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Diagnostic centres largely operate within partner hospital/PSU premises under MOUs (asset-light real-estate model), with the Company procuring, installing and maintaining its own diagnostic equipment (MRI, CT, X-ray, ultrasound, mammography, DEXA, PET-CT, etc.) and maintaining vendor relationships for procurement, pricing and fleet-wide maintenance. The Vijayawada processing unit-cum-laboratory and 24x7 teleradiology hub centralise sample processing and image reporting for centres across the network; in one West Bengal PSU arrangement the imaging equipment is instead provided by the PSU and diagnostic reporting is undertaken by them, with the Company's scope limited to operation and maintenance.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue mix shifting away from Andhra Pradesh concentration (84.78% in FY25 to 61.90% in FY26) as Karnataka and West Bengal centres ramp up
- EBITDA margin sensitive to service/partnership mix - contracted from 54.83% (FY25) to 49.61% (FY26) even as revenue grew
- Trade receivables linked to government/PSU counterparty payment cycles are a working-capital driver
- Growth in higher-value radiology sub-segments (CT, MRI, teleradiology) driving overall test volume and revenue growth

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expand geographic footprint by adding new diagnostic centres, including a proposed centre in Bangalore, Karnataka
- Continue investing in advanced diagnostic equipment and strengthening technology platform across centres
- Pursue unidentified inorganic acquisitions using general corporate purposes proceeds
- Deepen presence via diversified partnership models across public hospitals, private hospitals, PSUs and standalone centres

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Company intends to use IPO Net Proceeds to fund capex for medical equipment at a proposed new diagnostic centre in Bangalore (Karnataka), and to upgrade equipment at existing centres in Hubli (Karnataka), Manjeri (Kerala) and Vijayawada (Andhra Pradesh). Recent MOU/award wins have added centres in Madhya Pradesh (2026, via Notification of Award), West Bengal, Karnataka and Haryana/NCR Delhi (2025), and Kerala plus 3 centres in Uttar Pradesh (2024), taking the network to 16 centres across 7 states and 14 cities; a Kerala centre's machinery installation and a Karnataka cardiac-facility O&M project (Letter of Award received, MoU pending) had not yet commenced operations as of the DRHP date.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Strategic presence across 7 states of India (16 centres, 14 cities)
- Diversified network across four partnership models (PPP, Private-Private, PSU Strategic Partnership, standalone Private Centres)
- Technical capability with robust IT infrastructure and vendor relationships for equipment procurement
- Dedicated management team with significant industry experience
- Track record of revenue and financial performance
- Diverse customer-cum-patient base

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Concentration in Public Private Partnership MOUs with government authorities — 54.19% of FY26 revenue from PPP; non-renewal, modification or termination of MOUs, or payment delays from government counterparties, could materially affect the business
- Concentrated emphasis on radiology services — Radiology is the largest revenue-generating service line, exposing the company to segment-specific demand or technology risk
- Geographic revenue concentration in Andhra Pradesh — Andhra Pradesh still contributed 61.90% of FY26 revenue (down from 84.78% in FY25), leaving the company exposed to state-specific regulatory or demand shocks
- Trade receivables tied to hospital/government counterparties — Trade receivables of ₹1,740.05 lakhs (FY26) vs ₹1,117.49 lakhs (FY25) and ₹1,794.31 lakhs (FY24) create collection and liquidity risk

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Company plans to utilise Offer proceeds to fund capital expenditure for purchase of medical equipment at a proposed new diagnostic centre in Bangalore, Karnataka.**
- **Company intends to use Offer proceeds to purchase medical equipment at existing diagnostic centres in Hubli (Karnataka), Manjeri (Kerala) and Vijayawada (Andhra Pradesh).**
- **Company intends to use a portion of Net Proceeds for general corporate purposes and unidentified inorganic acquisition.**
- **Kerala centre installation of machinery yet to be completed; operations had not commenced as of March 31, 2026.**
- **Company has executed a Letter of Award from Government of Karnataka for operations and maintenance of a cardiac facility; the governing MoU is yet to be executed and the project has not commenced operations.**
- **Company has entered into a Notification of Award (NOA) in Madhya Pradesh for performing a medical imaging facility.**
- **Company continues to invest in advanced equipment and strengthen its technology platform across its diagnostic centres.**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand geographic footprint by adding new diagnostic centres, including a proposed centre in Bangalore, Karnataka
- Continue investing in advanced diagnostic equipment and strengthening technology platform across centres
- Pursue unidentified inorganic acquisitions using general corporate purposes proceeds
- Deepen presence via diversified partnership models across public hospitals, private hospitals, PSUs and standalone centres
